prompt: What was the strongest argument this speaker made, and why did it work?
Which argument needed a clearer link to the motion? What step in the reasoning was missing?
Did the evidence or example actually prove the point? What would have been more convincing?
Which of the other team's arguments did they answer best, and which did they leave standing?
Name one thing about their delivery that made the audience listen (eye contact, pace, pauses, voice).
Was there a moment where they rushed or read from notes? Suggest one specific change.
Did they sound like they believed it? Point to a moment that was persuasive, not just correct.
Could you tell their team line and their role in the team from the first minute?
Did the speech have a clear structure (signposting, a summary at the end)? Where did it lose shape?
Did they use their time well: about the right amount on rebuttal and on their own case?
Did the reply compare both teams' cases fairly, by theme, rather than repeating their own case?
Did the reply avoid new arguments?
Give the reason for the decision in one sentence a Year 7 could repeat.
Name the clash in the debate that decided it, and why one team won that clash.
Give each team one thing to do better next time. Be kind and specific; avoid 'be more confident'.
Speak to the speeches, not the speakers: say what was said and why it mattered.
